The Registered Nurse Oncology/Hematology is a clinical expert who uses advanced specialized knowledge and judgement for delivery of high quality and evidence-based care to oncology patients and their families. Uses a team approach to identify, analyze, and resolve patient care problems with measurable outcomes.

Completes physiological assessments and completes documentation in the electronic health record (EHR) in accordance to established policies and procedures. Triages patient problems and assists in the evaluation of symptoms and initiate interventions in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team.

Monitors, tracks/tends, and reports ongoing care needs and outcomes to the interdisciplinary team. They direct the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies, and providing quality improvement and outcome utilization.

They provide a safe working environment while administering, handling, and disposing of antineoplastic drugs and medical waste. They oversee the administration and management of various medical procedures and treatments in the oncology setting, including vascular access devices and infusion treatments.

Conducts in-service education based on insights gained from oncology professional development activities and acquiring specialized skills in oncology-specific areas, including chemotherapy administration, oncology electronic ordering systems, and calculating drug dosages.

The Oncology/Hematology RN manages monitoring requirements for specific drugs, handling immediate infusion reactions, and preventing and managing oncology-related symptoms and adverse events, such as chemo-related symptoms and immune-related adverse events.

Physical Requirements: This position potentially requires flexibility in schedule and assignments. This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear, distinctive speech, and manual dexterity. This position requires long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, kneeling, bending, pulling, and pushing.

Transferring patients and objects may be required. The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and must don protective clothing in isolation or during patient procedures and care. The incumbent may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

Use of fingers, both hands and near and far vision is required. Must complete annual Employee Health requirements, such as annual TB screening or testing, as a condition of employment.

The Registered Nurse (RN) Nurse Manager (NM) is the first-line supervisory authority accountable for the 24/7 operation of assigned units. They direct staff orientation, training, development, and evaluation while acting as a role model and supervisor.

The NM collaborates with interdisciplinary teams to enhance outcomes, ensures compliance with regulatory standards, and aligns clinical objectives with organizational strategic goals. Major duties include but are not limited to: Function as the designated first-line supervisory authority responsible for 24/7 unit operations.

Direct and supervise specific orientation, training, staff development, and individual performance evaluations. Functions as a clinical expert and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or supervising direct patient care.

Serve as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing team leadership. Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to remove barriers and implement evidence-based programs. Equip staff with tools for culturally competent care and promote accountability for high-quality outcomes.

Participate in the development of care delivery models and environmental design to ensure equitable care. Ensure compliance with all accreditation standards, regulatory requirements, and standard operating procedures. Align nursing and clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes and planning.

Promote an inclusive workplace that values diversity to achieve the organization's vision. Maintain knowledge of and ensure adherence to ethical principles in decision-making.

This is an approach to healthcare that empowers and equips people to take charge of their health and well-being and live their lives to the fullest.

As an employee operating in a Whole Health System of care, you will operate in a model with three core elements, seeking to create a personalized health plan for each Veteran. This is done in the context of healing relationships and healing environments and a connection back to the Veteran's community.

This aligns with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Mission Statement to Honor America's Veterans by providing exceptional health care that improves their health and well-being.

Utilize critical thinking skills to anticipate and respond to changes in patient conditions, initiating appropriate interventions and escalating concerns as necessary. Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings to ensure coordinated and holistic patient care.

La clinique Im Hasel AG est une clinique spécialisée en psychiatrie et psychothérapie avec un mandat cantonal pour le traitement des troubles liés à la dépendance et aux traumatismes. En tant qu'établissement reconnu par les caisses maladie et faisant partie de la liste cantonale des hôpitaux, nous offrons un traitement de haute qualité, fondé sur des preuves et humainement attentif à nos patient·e·s.
Avec environ 170 collaborateurs engagés sur trois sites - notre clinique stationnaire à Gontenschwil, l-ambulatorium et la clinique de jour à Lenzburg ainsi que l-ambulatorium spécialisé en traumatologie à Baden - nous allions compétence professionnelle et collaboration interdisciplinaire respectueuse.
Infirmier diplômé HF/FH (h/f/d) 100%
Nous recherchons dès maintenant ou selon accord un soutien pour notre équipe soignante sur le site de Gontenschwil.

* Soins médicaux et infirmiers de nos patient·e·s (hors soins de base) sur tous les postes
* Direction et développement des offres de groupe / groupes indicatifs
* Prise en charge des patient·e·s en tant que personne de référence selon le concept interne DBT-dépendance
* Participation aux rapports interdisciplinaires, visites, réunions d-équipe et entretiens sur site
* Contribution à la mise en œuvre et au développement des standards de soins et du concept thérapeutique
* Accompagnement des étudiant·e·s et apprenti·e·s en pratique
* Prise en charge de responsabilités au sein des soins
Votre profil
* Diplôme d-infirmier diplômé HF/FH (AKP, DNII, PsyKP)
* Expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de la dépendance et/ou en psychiatrie souhaitée
* Flexibilité, intégrité, équilibre et patience comptent parmi vos forces
* Vous vous décrivez comme une personne ouverte, motivée, responsable, résistante au stress et capable de travailler en équipe
* La discrétion et la fiabilité sont pour vous une évidence
* Permis de conduire voiture incluant véhicule (pas de liaison transports publics en travail posté) Nous attendons une attitude marquée par le respect et la considération dans le contact avec nos patient·e·s.

Die Spitäler Schaffhausen als Arbeitgeber
Die Spitäler Schaffhausen umfassen das Kantonsspital, die Psychiatrischen Dienste, die Praxen Radiologie und Kardiologie Posthof Neuhausen sowie die Praxis Neurologie Schaffhausen Zentrum. Mit über 1'700 Mitarbeitenden sichern wir die erweiterte medizinische und pflegerische Grundversorgung der Region Schaffhausen. Jährlich betreuen wir etwa 11'000 stationäre und 90'000 ambulante Patientinnen und Patienten. Zudem sind wir eine wichtige Ausbildungsstätte im Kanton.
Für unsere Heroingestützte Behandlung (HeGeBe) der psychiatrischen Dienste suchen wir per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung ein/e Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/mann HF, Fachfrau/\-mann Gesundheit oder Medizinische Praxisassistent/in.
Das HeGeBe (heroingestützten Behandlung) Schaffhausen ist eines von 23 Behandlungszentren in der Schweiz. Das HeGeBe bietet ambulante Opioid\-Agonisten\-Therapien an und unterstützt Menschen mit Abhängigkeitserkrankungen bei der Verbesserung der somatischen, psychiatrischen und sozialen Situation, der Verhinderung von Infektionen wie HIV oder Hepatitis, der Reduktion von Straffälligkeiten sowie der langfristige Abstinenz von nicht\-verschriebenen Substanzen.

For Nurse, GS-0610-12: Communicates and coordinates with health care providers to assess appropriate levels of home health care to ensure the care the claimant receives reflects the policies and procedures of DEEOIC.

Coordinates and conducts outreach and training to medical providers and other stakeholders, program staff, other Federal Agencies, and the general public.

Under the direction and leadership of the Lead Nurse and Unit Manager, the employee plans and implements assignments, projects, and/or studies in the areas of home health care, durable medical equipment, and other medical issues.

Utilizes current medical and scientific knowledge, medical journals, reference manuals, books, the DEEOIC Procedure Manual and related policy, and other resources to develop rationale for his/her opinions.

Provides input for accurate application of medical guidelines to the processing of medical services by serving as a resource for medical billing issues. The employee develops training materials for DEEOIC staff, health care providers, and beneficiaries.

Works with the Medical Bill Pay staff or other National Office staff to monitor procedures and evaluate their validity and cost-effectiveness by the utilization of models from Medicare and other federal agencies.

Within the assigned area, determines medical appropriateness of requested ancillary procedures and/or services that require authorization by senior management.

Education - Transcripts must be submitted with your application package.

A graduate or higher level degree, bachelor's degree, associate degree, or diploma from an accredited professional nursing educational program is required.

Department of Education (external link) at the time the degree was obtained. Degree from Foreign Nursing School: Official certification from the Commission on Graduates of Foreign Nursing Schools (external link) is required for individuals who graduated from foreign nursing schools.

Licensure - A copy of your license must be submitted with your application package. If you have recently renewed your license, please submit renewal documentation. For all grade levels and positions, applicants must have passed the National Council Licensure Examination (external link).

In addition, they must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a professional nurse from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

Additional License Requirements for Advanced Practice Nurse Positions: Applicants for Advanced Practice Nurse positions must be licensed or registered by a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States in the clinical specialty required by the position. *** In addition to the mandatory license and education described above under Basic Requirements applicants must have at least one or more full years of professional nursing experience that is equivalent to the next lower grade level. *** Applicants must have 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, GS-11 in the Federal Service.

Specialized Experience is the experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSA's) to perform the duties of the position successfully, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level.

Qualifying specialized experience for GS-12 includes: Experience reviewing and evaluating complex medical evidence, including medical records, physician reports, treatment plans, and medical/scientific literature, to determine medical necessity or appropriateness of health-care services and prepare clinically supported assessments or recommendations.

Experience applying medical policies, health-care guidelines, and claims or medical-billing requirements to resolve medical issues associated with claims adjudication, authorization of medical services, home health care, durable medical equipment, or other health-care benefits.

Experience developing, analyzing, or evaluating medical policies, guidelines, standards, or procedures, including assessing their clinical validity, effectiveness, utilization or cost-effectiveness, and recommending or implementing program improvements.

Experience providing professional medical consultation and technical assistance to internal and external stakeholders, including coordinating with health-care providers, advising claims or program staff on complex medical matters, and developing or delivering medical-policy training and outreach.

Description de l'entreprise
Ancrée dans le panorama de la Riviera depuis 1905, la Clinique Valmont offre des séjours de réadaptation personnalisés pour les personnes présentant des atteintes neurologiques, orthopédiques et du dos, dans un cadre exceptionnel, face au Lac Léman et aux Alpes.

Aujourd'hui, elle est devenue un établissement phare dans la réadaptation, de par son efficience thérapeutique inégalée, ses équipes compétentes et son plateau technique de pointe.

En effet, les médecins en réadaptation collaborent avec une équipe d'experts multidisciplinaires, composée de physiothérapeutes, ergothérapeutes, neuropsychologues, logopédistes, maîtres de sport et diététicienne. En 2006, la clinique a rejoint Swiss Medical Network, l'un des deux principaux groupes suisses de cliniques privées.
Description du poste
En tant qu'ICUS, vous assurez un rôle clé dans l'organisation et le pilotage des activités de soins au sein de la clinique de réadaptation.

Participez activement à la gestion de l'équipe soignante (planification, encadrement, accompagnement des collaborateurs, gestion des priorités).
Veillez à la fluidité, à la qualité et à la fiabilité des informations transmises au sein de l'établissement et entre les différents acteurs de la prise en charge.
Garantissez l'efficience de la prise en charge des patients, en assurant une organisation optimale des ressources et une répartition adéquate de la charge de travail.
Assurez la qualité et la sécurité des soins, dans le respect des normes, protocoles et exigences institutionnelles.
Contribuez au développement, à l'optimisation et à l'harmonisation des processus de soins.
Participez à la mise en place, à l'évaluation et au suivi des protocoles de réadaptation, en collaboration avec les équipes pluridisciplinaires.
Soutenez les équipes sur le terrain et intervenez dans les situations complexes.
Favorisez un climat de travail positif et une dynamique d'équipe constructive.
